items.title: Darius Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 29, 2024
items.q: we mentioned his name earlier with Zim Ngqawana — we co-composed it

ctx.x: When you sit down to write if you have a goal, a specific goal in mind of — you wrote a song for his 80th birthday and you wrote something performed at Lincoln Center, do you approach this composition work differently than if you’re just — you’re in the mood to write, you sit and wait for something to happen. Is there a different approach depending on the goal?

Oh absolutely. There’s — look in terms of waiting for something to happen if I just come up with a phrase when I’m practicing — some things don’t come from the brain, they come from the fingers you know. And it won’t be — in my case — I’m not that brilliant that it will be complete but it will be enough to say gosh you know if I develop this, if I extend it, if I, you know, you would know all the manipulations that are possible you know I’ve actually got something. That’s one thing. If I’m — and then you referred…

Mandela and Archbishop Desmond Tutu. All of the other commissions were also musical settings from speeches — oh Billy Childs was another one. But anyway, get the facts because it’s fascinating. I don’t want to be responsible in this interview for naming everyone and getting everything exact.
